claims.claim: The Four Pests campaign targeted rats, flies, mosquitoes, and sparrows for elimination.
claims.episode_span: Sparrows appeared on the pest list because they consumed grain seeds and ripening crops; the other three targets were rats, flies, and mosquitoes
claims.supporting_quote: Authorities targeted four " pests " for elimination: rats , flies , mosquitoes , and sparrows .

claims.claim: The campaign was one of the first campaigns of the Great Leap Forward, running from 1958.
claims.episode_span: The Four Pests Campaign emerged inside the Great Leap Forward, Mao Zedong’s 1958 drive to transform China from an agrarian country into an industrial power
claims.supporting_quote: was one of the first campaigns of the Great Leap Forward in Maoist China from 1958 to 1962

claims.claim: Exterminating sparrows upset the ecological balance and led to surging locust and other insect populations that destroyed crops.
claims.episode_span: With sparrow populations collapsed, locust and other insect numbers rose sharply in 1959 and 1960
claims.supporting_quote: [ 38 ] [ 39 ] The extermination of sparrows upset the ecological balance , which subsequently resulted in surging locust and other insect populations that destroyed crops due to a lack of a natural predator.

claims.claim: The sparrow extermination was one contributing cause — among several — of the Great Chinese Famine of 1959-1961.
claims.episode_span: The loss of an avian predator was only one factor among many that produced the 1959–1961 famine
claims.supporting_quote: resulted in severe ecological imbalance, and was one of the causes of the Great Chinese Famine which lasted from 1959 to 1961

claims.claim: In 1960 the campaign against sparrows was ended and bed bugs replaced them as an official target.
claims.episode_span: In March 1960 the central government quietly removed sparrows from the Four Pests list and substituted bed bugs
claims.supporting_quote: In 1960, the campaign against sparrows ended, and bed bugs replaced them as an official target.

claims.claim: After the campaign left the Eurasian tree sparrow nearly extinct in China, the country imported 250,000 sparrows from the Soviet Union to rebuild the population.
claims.episode_span: Some provinces began importing sparrows from the Soviet Union and Mongolia to restore populations
claims.supporting_quote: the Eurasian tree sparrow was practically extinct from China, which afterwards imported 250,000 Eurasian tree sparrows from the Soviet Union to recover its population.

claims.claim: Chinese scientists' warnings mattered: ornithologist Tso-hsin Cheng's evidence that sparrows ate large numbers of insects helped change party leaders' opinion of the campaign.
claims.episode_span: Some agronomists inside the Chinese Academy of Sciences quietly noted that sparrows also ate large numbers of locusts and other insects
claims.supporting_quote: changed their opinion on the Eliminate Sparrows campaign in part due to the influence of ornithologist Tso-hsin Cheng
